{
  "findings": [

      "category": "security",
      "title": "Webhook secret is compared with ===",
      "body": "The endpoint authenticates requests by comparing the incoming header to process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using JavaScript equality. String equality can short-circuit and may be vulnerable to timing analysis, allowing an attacker to gradually infer the secret. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual on fixed-length buffers after verifying both values exist."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Credential upsert is not atomic and can create duplicates",
      "body": "The handler searches for an existing credential with findFirst and then creates or updates it in separate queries. There is no transaction or unique constraint on (userId, appId). Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss an existing row and insert duplicates, or if duplicates already exist findFirst may update an arbitrary row. This can leave users with multiple/stale credentials and app adapters may use the wrong one."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 31,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Malformed webhook payloads cause unhandled errors",
      "body": "appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse can all throw. The handler does not catch these errors, so malformed payloads produce an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. These should be caught and returned as validation errors."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 17,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Webhook accepts all HTTP methods",
      "body": "The API route does not check req.method, so any HTTP method is processed. It should only accept POST, or the documented method, and return 405 for others."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "minimumTokenResponseSchema is not a valid permissive Zod schema",
      "body": "The schema uses computed keys such as [z.string().toString()] to try to allow arbitrary properties. This creates literal property names from the schema's string representation rather than a catchall or record schema, so it will either require nonsensical keys or strip expected fields such as expires_in. In app-credential syncing mode this can reject valid token responses or remove expiry data before saving credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 26,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal placeholder",
      "body": "If a token response does not include refresh_token, the code sets it to the literal string 'refresh_token'. This placeholder can be persisted into credential.key and later sent to OAuth providers, making future refreshes fail and corrupting the credential. Missing refresh tokens should preserve the existing refresh token or mark the credential invalid, not insert a fake value."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 22,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "parseRefreshTokenResponse throws despite callers expecting safeParse result",
      "body": "The helper calls safeParse but then throws an Error when validation fails, while several callers still check .success to handle invalid tokens gracefully. This changes the contract and turns recoverable invalid-token responses into unhandled exceptions or bypasses intended error handling in apps such as Zoom and Salesforce."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Sync path returns a fetch Response while callers expect parsed tokens",
      "body": "When credential syncing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Existing callers are written to receive the same type as the provider refresh function: Google expects a response object with .data, HubSpot expects a parsed token object with accessToken/expiresIn, and Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM expect an AxiosResponse with .data. In sync mode these callers will read undefined properties, compute NaN expiries, or throw TypeErrors, breaking token refresh for those apps."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Zoho Bigin sends credential ID as calcomUserId",
      "body": "refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId, the credential's primary key, as the third argument. refreshOAuthTokens then sends that value as calcomUserId to the credential sync endpoint. The sync endpoint will receive a credential ID instead of the Cal.com user ID, so it can return tokens for the wrong user or fail. credential.userId should be passed instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "prisma is used but never imported",
      "body": "The new token-refresh code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will cause a ReferenceError at runtime, and likely a TypeScript/build error, whenever Salesforce credential refresh is attempted."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Salesforce connection is created with the old access token after refresh",
      "body": "getClient refreshes the Salesforce token and stores the new token in the database, but then returns a jsforce.Connection using credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url from the old credential object. The newly fetched access token is not used, so if the old token was expired the next API calls still fail. Use the parsed refresh response's access_token and instance_url."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Salesforce client refreshes token on every instantiation",
      "body": "getClient performs an OAuth token refresh every time a SalesforceCalendarService is constructed, regardless of whether the existing access token is still valid. Calendar operations instantiate services frequently, which can cause unnecessary calls to Salesforce, rate limiting, and increased latency. The token expiry should be checked before refreshing."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 188,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Zoho CRM token validity check is inverted",
      "body": "isTokenValid treats expiryDate < Date.now() as valid, which is true only after the token has expired. getToken resolves without refreshing when isTokenValid is true and refreshes when it is false, so expired tokens are used and unexpired tokens trigger refreshes. The expiry is also set using Date.now() + 60 * 60, which is only a few seconds in milliseconds, making the problem worse."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Credential sync request has no authentication or signature",
      "body": "The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT only sends calcomUserId and appSlug; it does not include a shared secret, signature, or other authentication. If the sync endpoint is reachable, it may be possible to request or rotate tokens based on unauthenticated requests. Add a configurable secret/signature header and verify it on the external app store."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 17,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No automated tests for privileged credential-sync webhook",
      "body": "The PR introduces a webhook that can create or update arbitrary user credentials, plus multiple token-refresh code paths, but no tests are included. At minimum, tests should cover secret verification, disabled feature behavior, malformed or undecryptable payloads, duplicate credential handling, and sync-enabled refresh flows."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Webhook secret is compared with ===
findings.body: The endpoint authenticates requests by comparing the incoming header to process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using JavaScript equality. String equality can short-circuit and may be vulnerable to timing analysis, allowing an attacker to gradually infer the secret. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual on fixed-length buffers after verifying both values exist.

findings.title: Credential upsert is not atomic and can create duplicates
findings.body: The handler searches for an existing credential with findFirst and then creates or updates it in separate queries. There is no transaction or unique constraint on (userId, appId). Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss an existing row and insert duplicates, or if duplicates already exist findFirst may update an arbitrary row. This can leave users with multiple/stale credentials and app adapters may use the wrong one.

findings.title: Malformed webhook payloads cause unhandled errors
findings.body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse can all throw. The handler does not catch these errors, so malformed payloads produce an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. These should be caught and returned as validation errors.

findings.title: Webhook accepts all HTTP methods
findings.body: The API route does not check req.method, so any HTTP method is processed. It should only accept POST, or the documented method, and return 405 for others.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema is not a valid permissive Zod schema
findings.body: The schema uses computed keys such as [z.string().toString()] to try to allow arbitrary properties. This creates literal property names from the schema's string representation rather than a catchall or record schema, so it will either require nonsensical keys or strip expected fields such as expires_in. In app-credential syncing mode this can reject valid token responses or remove expiry data before saving credentials.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal placeholder
findings.body: If a token response does not include refresh_token, the code sets it to the literal string 'refresh_token'. This placeholder can be persisted into credential.key and later sent to OAuth providers, making future refreshes fail and corrupting the credential. Missing refresh tokens should preserve the existing refresh token or mark the credential invalid, not insert a fake value.

findings.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws despite callers expecting safeParse result
findings.body: The helper calls safeParse but then throws an Error when validation fails, while several callers still check .success to handle invalid tokens gracefully. This changes the contract and turns recoverable invalid-token responses into unhandled exceptions or bypasses intended error handling in apps such as Zoom and Salesforce.

findings.title: Sync path returns a fetch Response while callers expect parsed tokens
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Existing callers are written to receive the same type as the provider refresh function: Google expects a response object with .data, HubSpot expects a parsed token object with accessToken/expiresIn, and Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM expect an AxiosResponse with .data. In sync mode these callers will read undefined properties, compute NaN expiries, or throw TypeErrors, breaking token refresh for those apps.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends credential ID as calcomUserId
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId, the credential's primary key, as the third argument. refreshOAuthTokens then sends that value as calcomUserId to the credential sync endpoint. The sync endpoint will receive a credential ID instead of the Cal.com user ID, so it can return tokens for the wrong user or fail. credential.userId should be passed instead.

findings.title: prisma is used but never imported
findings.body: The new token-refresh code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will cause a ReferenceError at runtime, and likely a TypeScript/build error, whenever Salesforce credential refresh is attempted.

findings.title: Salesforce connection is created with the old access token after refresh
findings.body: getClient refreshes the Salesforce token and stores the new token in the database, but then returns a jsforce.Connection using credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url from the old credential object. The newly fetched access token is not used, so if the old token was expired the next API calls still fail. Use the parsed refresh response's access_token and instance_url.

findings.title: Salesforce client refreshes token on every instantiation
findings.body: getClient performs an OAuth token refresh every time a SalesforceCalendarService is constructed, regardless of whether the existing access token is still valid. Calendar operations instantiate services frequently, which can cause unnecessary calls to Salesforce, rate limiting, and increased latency. The token expiry should be checked before refreshing.

findings.title: Zoho CRM token validity check is inverted
findings.body: isTokenValid treats expiryDate < Date.now() as valid, which is true only after the token has expired. getToken resolves without refreshing when isTokenValid is true and refreshes when it is false, so expired tokens are used and unexpired tokens trigger refreshes. The expiry is also set using Date.now() + 60 * 60, which is only a few seconds in milliseconds, making the problem worse.

findings.title: Credential sync request has no authentication or signature
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT only sends calcomUserId and appSlug; it does not include a shared secret, signature, or other authentication. If the sync endpoint is reachable, it may be possible to request or rotate tokens based on unauthenticated requests. Add a configurable secret/signature header and verify it on the external app store.

findings.title: No automated tests for privileged credential-sync webhook
findings.body: The PR introduces a webhook that can create or update arbitrary user credentials, plus multiple token-refresh code paths, but no tests are included. At minimum, tests should cover secret verification, disabled feature behavior, malformed or undecryptable payloads, duplicate credential handling, and sync-enabled refresh flows.
